title: GitHub Pays $100,000 Bounty for Critical RCE Flaw Triggered by a Single Git Push
content_md: GitHub has reportedly awarded a $100,000 bug bounty to security researcher Saif Ghani for identifying a critical remote code execution vulnerability that could be triggered through a specially crafted Git repository operation. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-3854, was disclosed publicly on July 22 after GitHub remediated the issue through its coordinated vulnerability disclosure process. The reported vulnerability affected GitHub’s handling of crafted repository URLs or Git push-related input. An attacker could allegedly abuse the vulnerable processing path to execute arbitrary commands on GitHub backend infrastructure without prior authentication. GitHub Pays $100,000 Bounty for Critical RCE Flaw Remote code execution vulnerabilities are among the highest-impact bugs for source-code hosting platforms because a successful exploit can move beyond a single repository or user account. If attackers obtain command execution within a platform’s backend environment, they may attempt to access internal services, manipulate source-code delivery workflows, retrieve sensitive credentials, or interfere with build and deployment pipelines. RuntimeWire said the proof of concept resulted in shell access on an affected server environment. From there, researchers showed the potential to read repository secrets and alter code while the service handled it. That scenario creates a particularly serious software supply-chain concern.
